narrative:
The 2023 Chicago Cubs were a team of contradictions — potent enough to score 819 runs and slug 196 home runs, yet maddeningly inconsistent when it mattered most. They stumbled out of April at .500, then cratered in May with a 10-18 record that threatened to bury their season before the summer heat arrived. The bullpen leaked and the lineup went cold at the worst moments, and the high-leverage plays from those early months read like a highlight reel of Cubs heartbreak: pitchers surrendering clutch singles, batters grounding into double plays with runners on, and opposing hitters feasting on relief pitching.

June brought a steadying 14-11 mark, and then July ignited something real. The Cubs went 15-11 in July, fueled by a string of late-game heroics — Ian Happ gunning down a runner at the plate, Mike Tauchman delivering a go-ahead double, and the infield turning double plays at critical moments to preserve leads. August was the Cubs' best month, a dazzling 18-9 run that briefly made the playoff dream feel tangible. Christopher Morel's three-run bomb in mid-August was the exclamation point on the surge, a moment that captured everything this team could be when firing on all cylinders.

But September exposed the Cubs' fatal flaw: they simply couldn't close. A 12-16 September collapse, punctuated by Adbert Alzolay surrendering a homer to open the month, repeated bullpen implosions against the Reds and Diamondbacks, and a costly Seiya Suzuki error against Atlanta that let two runs score, drained the life from their playoff hopes. The team that had charged to within striking distance with August's brilliance stumbled across the finish line at 83-79, watching the wild card door slam shut.

In the end, the 2023 Cubs were a tantalizing near-miss. Their offense was legitimate and their mid-season surge was genuine, but an inability to win the close games in September — precisely when a playoff push demands it — left them watching October from home. The pieces are there for something special; whether they can add the consistency to match the potential remains the defining question heading into 2024.

chapters.title: False Starts and Early Stumbles
chapters.description: The Cubs limp through April and an ugly May, with high-leverage failures piling up and the season already feeling like an uphill climb.

chapters.title: May Malaise
chapters.description: A brutal 10-18 May sees the Cubs ground into double plays and give up clutch hits, falling dangerously behind in the wild card race.

chapters.title: Midsummer Momentum
chapters.description: June stabilizes the ship, and July catches fire with back-to-back clutch plays over the Brewers that signal the Cubs are for real.

chapters.title: The August Surge
chapters.description: The Cubs' best baseball arrives in August — an 18-9 tear capped by Morel's three-run blast — making the playoff dream feel real.

chapters.title: September Collapse
chapters.description: The bullpen unravels and the offense goes quiet as a 12-16 September extinguishes Chicago's wild card hopes one painful loss at a time.
